candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 21:22-23. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Cf. Gal 3:13 (verbatim Pauline citation).
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'he that is hanged is accursed of God' (Deu 21:23), Ephrem reads the curse-on-the-hanged-corpse statute as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of Paul's atonement-formula in Galatians 3:13: 'Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree' — verbatim citation. The Deuteronomic curse is not abolished but absorbed: Christ takes the curse upon himself precisely by hanging on the tree. Tewahedo atonement theology cites Deu 21:23 + Gal 3:13 as the canonical doubled-anchor of the substitutionary cross — the Cross is canonical-curse-bearing, the Christ is canonical-curse-bearer, the redemption is canonical-completion.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'he that is hanged is accursed of God' (Deu 21:23), Ephrem reads the curse-on-the-hanged-corpse statute as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of Paul's atonement-formula in Galatians 3:13: 'Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree' — verbatim citation. The Deuteronomic curse is not abolished but absorbed: Christ takes the curse upon himself precisely by hanging on the tree. Tewahedo atonement theology cites Deu 21:23 + Gal 3:13 as the canonical doubled-anchor of the substitutionary cross — the Cross is canonical-curse-bearing, the Christ is canonical-curse-bearer, the redemption is canonical-completion.
